text:
Situation: Epinephrine has been on FDA's shortage list since 2012-02-22 and remains Current as of 2026-10-21. Current inventory across three sites ranges from 3.3 to 25 days of supply, with the lowest coverage at Corvale East for the 0.3 mg/0.3 mL syringe (21 units, 3.3 days).

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the shortage on 2012-02-22. A Hospira, Inc. inspection (FEI 1925262) ended 2012-01-04 with VAI classification, 49 days before the posting. The same plant received OAI classifications after inspections ending 2016-06-08 and 2018-08-15; the latter classification was known by FDA on 2020-04-22. An import alert 66-66 for Boehringer Ingelheim Pharma GmbH & Co. KG (FEI 3002806556) was published 2009-09-30, 875 days before the shortage posting. That Boehringer plant was inspected and classified OAI on 2012-11-12, 264 days after the shortage posting.

Our position: Supply is critically low for multiple presentations. The rule‑based best option is Viatris Specialty LLC, which is not on FDA's shortage list today. Four additional suppliers also are not on the shortage list.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer initiates purchase from Viatris Specialty LLC; requires Pharmacy Director approval.
2. Buyer qualifies kaleo, Inc. as secondary source; requires Pharmacy Director approval.
3. Buyer evaluates Advanced Rx Pharmacy of Tennessee, LLC, American Regent, Inc., and Amneal Pharmaceuticals LLC for formulary addition; requires P&T Committee approval.
4. Buyer allocates incoming stock to Corvale East first; requires Operations Manager approval.

Not recommended: Delaying procurement pending further FDA updates; relying solely on current Hospira or Boehringer supply given their inspection histories.
